newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies post closing gains on USDA.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies post closing gains on USDA.

text.p: A bullish USDA Hogs and Pigs Report Thursday and forecasts for greater pork exports this summer sparked limit gains in deferred CME lean hog futures and sharply higher CME pork belly futures, traders said.
CME May pork bellies briefly touched the 3.00-cent-per-lb upper limit late on buying by Cargill, but late local selling near the close trimmed that gain, traders said.

Gains in CME April lean hogs were restricted by fund liquidation and bear spreading with June. Gains in June, July and August were attributed to USDA's reporting of 475,000 fewer hogs kept for marketing as of March 1 than a year ago.

Ample hog supplies for immediate slaughter has Dan Vaught, analyst with A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc, bearish on near-term hog cash and futures prices. He said hog weights last week were up from a year ago and pork output was up 1.2 percent from the previous week and up 3.5 percent from a year ago.
USDA reported the average weight of slaughter hogs last week at 256 lbs, the same as the previous week but slightly up from 255 lbs in the comparable week a year ago.
